title: On linearity or non-linearity in machine learning for quantum chaotic dynamics
authors: Francesco Perciavalle, Agostino Gallo, Francesco Plastina, Gianluigi Greco, Nicola Lo Gullo, Carlo Adornetto
abstract: Accurately simulating chaotic quantum many-body dynamics remains a major computational challenge for classical methods, due to the rapid buildup and spatial spreading of entanglement during the evolution. This raises the question of whether machine learning can provide an effective alternative for predicting quantum dynamics. We address this question by formulating quantum dynamics as a time-series forecasting problem, using a few-qubit PXP chain, realizable with Rydberg-atom arrays, as a benchmark. By varying the initial state, the system spans dynamical regimes ranging from ergodic behavior to quantum many-body scarring, providing a controlled setting for testing forecasting models across qualitatively different dynamics. We compare two contrasting architectures: an expressive nonlinear Transformer and DLinear, a simple linear forecasting model. The Transformer accurately predicts dynamics in the more ergodic regime, but its performance progressively deteriorates as the initial state approaches the scarred limit. In contrast, DLinear remains accurate across the entire family of initial states, with its main deviations consisting of small high-frequency oscillations that have little effect on the overall prediction error. Remarkably, these results show that observables generated by complex quantum many-body dynamics can be forecast with high accuracy through a simple linear mapping from past to future observations. This reveals that the complexity of the underlying quantum evolution need not translate into an equally complex forecasting problem.
summary: This work tackles the difficulty of simulating chaotic quantum many-body systems by framing the problem as time-series forecasting. By comparing a nonlinear Transformer to a linear model (DLinear) on a Rydberg-atom-based PXP model, the authors show that the simple linear model maintains high accuracy across all dynamical regimes, even those exhibiting complex quantum scarring. This suggests that the underlying quantum complexity is not necessarily reflected in the complexity required for prediction.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational challenge of simulating chaotic quantum many-body dynamics and investigates if Machine Learning can provide an effective alternative for predicting these complex time evolutions.
main_result: Simple linear forecasting models (DLinear) can accurately predict observables generated by complex quantum dynamics across various regimes, suggesting that the complexity of the evolution does not necessitate an equally complex forecasting model.
method: The authors formulate quantum dynamics as a time-series forecasting problem, comparing the performance of a nonlinear Transformer against a simple linear model (DLinear) on simulated quantum trajectories.
model_or_system: The study uses the paradigmatic PXP model, simulating dynamics on a few-qubit chain realizable with Rydberg-atom arrays. The system is tested across dynamical regimes ranging from ergodic behavior to non-ergodic quantum many-body scarring.
key_observables: Local magnetizations and connected two-point correlation functions are used as the feature vectors for time-series forecasting.
important_parameters: The initial state choice controls the dynamical regime, parameterized between fully polarized and Néel states. The analysis compares performance across these controlled initial conditions.
main_assumptions: The framework is benchmarked on a few-qubit PXP chain where exact time evolution is computable, but the methodology is claimed to be extendable to other systems with available time-series data.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the data preparation, training, and prediction stages for both the Transformer and DLinear models across different initial states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting the difficulty of simulating chaotic dynamics, details the ML forecasting protocol using the PXP model, compares the Transformer and DLinear architectures across varying initial states, and concludes by demonstrating the superior performance of the linear model.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, data-driven test case showing that linear ML methods can capture the essential dynamics of highly complex, non-integrable quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding information extraction from quantum chaos.

Data preparation (a): A set of N initial quantum states, {|ψk⟩}N k=1, of an L-qubit system is prepared. Each state is evolved under the Hamiltonian ˆHPXP, generating N quantum trajectories, {|ψk(t)⟩}N k=1. At each time t, each trajectory is represented by a feature vector xk(t) comprising local magnetizations and connected two-point correlations, for a total of F = L(L + 1)/2 features.
